world.bio: I coordinate a weaving cooperative of twenty-two women in a mountain district three hours from Chiang Mai. Our members work backstrap looms and floor looms; the patterns are Karen, handed down from grandmothers. I handle the orders by phone from the one spot in the village where there is signal, which is a flat rock behind the temple.
skills_assets: Cooperative of 22 weavers, backstrap and floor loom, natural-dye cotton and hemp
Pattern archive in a school exercise book: about 60 traditional Karen motifs
A shared workshop with six floor looms, funded by an NGO in 2021
A small list of buyers in Chiang Mai and two in Bangkok
Spoken Karen, Thai, English good enough for orders and emails

projects.name: Autumn orders
projects.text: Twelve shawls for a boutique in Chiang Mai, due mid-October. Three weavers are behind because of rice harvest preparation.

projects.name: Natural dye experiments
projects.text: Testing indigo and lac on hemp. We've had two batches that came out blotchy; the third looks promising.

projects.name: Village temple fair
projects.text: Helping organise the fair in November. We hope to run a small stall for the weavers.

projects.name: Grant report to the NGO
projects.text: The NGO that paid for the workshop wants a year-end report: orders, income per weaver, new designs. I keep these numbers in a school notebook and have to type them up on someone else's phone.

notes.text: Rain every afternoon. The looms are quiet in the workshop. The rainy season means most of the women are in the fields, then in the rice paddies, and then in the kitchens. We rarely get more than six looms running at once. In the months after planting the looms sit mostly idle.

Climbed the rock behind the temple to call a buyer. Signal was one bar. Spent ten minutes saying 'hello, can you hear me' to a boutique owner in Chiang Mai. She said she could hear me about half the time. We settled on the colour by sending photographs.

Mae Bua's cut on her hand was swollen again this morning. She said it is nothing. I made her go to the temple's herbalist. Last season two weavers had infected cuts and one needed antibiotics. The nearest clinic is ninety minutes away and nobody in the village knows basic wound care.

Son called from Chiang Mai. He is studying agriculture and said the professor wants him to do a project on soil in the mountains. I told him come home in November, you can do your project here. He said yes, but I could hear that he was already thinking about something else.
Counted the thread. We are short of undyed hemp. The supplier says two weeks. I said we have orders. He said then you have to wait.
The village headman asked if the cooperative could host guests from a travel agency. I said we are not a hotel. He said the guests would pay for the experience. I said I'd ask the women.
The temple fair meeting. I was asked to bring a speech about our weaving. I said I'm a coordinator, not a speaker. The abbot said just speak plainly. I practised in the shower.
Finished a shawl myself, the first in three years. The pattern is my grandmother's, a zigzag in indigo and white. I held it up to the light and thought, this is why we do it.

messages.text:
Owner: Naw, can you do twelve in the same blue?
Me: We can try.
Owner: Mid-October?
Me: Yes, if the dye is steady.

Saw: Mum, can you send me money for the lab fee?
Me: How much?
Saw: 1,200 baht.
Me: I'll send it tomorrow.

Headman: The travel agent will bring six guests on 20 October.
Me: What will they do?
Headman: Watch the weaving and have lunch.
Me: We will think about it.

Mae Bua: Coordinator, my hand is better.
Me: Good. Keep it clean.
Mae Bua: The herbalist gave me leaves.
Me: Keep the leaves, but also keep it clean.

Officer: Naw, the grant report is due on 30 October.
Me: I will send the photos.
Officer: Please include the number of orders.
Me: Seventeen so far this year.

calendar.event: Travel agency guests visit the workshop

relations.about: Studying agriculture at a university in Chiang Mai
One of the oldest weavers, stubborn about her injuries
Wants the village to earn more from visitors

constraints: Looms cannot run during the rice harvest in November
Natural dyes only, no chemical dyes
Does not want the cooperative to become a tourist show
sensitive: Worries the cooperative will lose young women to factory work
Money is tight; the NGO funding ends next year
Her own daughter left for a factory job in Bangkok last year and calls rarely
